title: Restore of a platform's own lost-link values isn't retried when its link returns, while the queue dispatches then
description: Final review of rules 6 on the queue (c1c4d78), crates/murmur-bridge/src/decision/engage.rs around lines 587 and 702. After an engagement ends, restoring the platform's own lost-link values backs off; a probe (abort, then a 10-minute outage) had 6 failed restores and the restore confirmed only 220 s after the link returned (up to 300 s). Queued orders for that platform go out on the first tick after the link returns, so for minutes the platform still carries the ended engagement's lost-link action with its short timer (5 s; copter abort fallback BRAKE, else LAND). A second short gap on the same flaky link then brakes, lands or returns the vehicle instead of its own 30-120 s SATCOM failsafe, cutting the dequeued order short (ends unconfirmed, goes to a human). The inbox does show restore_pending. Fix: retry the restore as soon as the platform is heard again after silence, or restore before releasing a dequeued order to a platform still owed values.
close_reason: Merged as decision rules 7 (QUEUE_FOLLOWUPS_SINCE) after review, re-check and a third check: starts logged ahead; missions held (or refused for never-queued kinds) while a platform is owed its own lost-link values; an order queued, dispatched or refused for an engaging platform supersedes it without fallback; engine refuses requeue after a start; airship refusal text corrected.

title: Queue: a crash within ~1 s of a start loses 'may have started'
description: Third review of the safe command queue (604e2c0). The 'starting' op is logged only at the next decision tick (crates/murmur-bridge/src/decision/mod.rs, around line 1517), so a bridge crash inside that window leaves no record that the start went out. The reviewer's probe N6 restarted a mission over a failsafe RTL after such a crash. Fix: write 'starting' before the start goes out, or treat 'held, not running, in a failsafe mode' as may-have-started on carry-over.
close_reason: Merged as decision rules 7 (QUEUE_FOLLOWUPS_SINCE) after review, re-check and a third check: starts logged ahead; missions held (or refused for never-queued kinds) while a platform is owed its own lost-link values; an order queued, dispatched or refused for an engaging platform supersedes it without fallback; engine refuses requeue after a start; airship refusal text corrected.

title: Space segment: taskable satellites as infrastructure (coverage, collection, SATCOM)
description: Satellites as taskable infrastructure, not flown nodes. The operator asks for a capability over an area and time window (imagery/SAR collection, SATCOM coverage or capacity, GNSS assurance); the system computes feasible passes from real orbits (SGP4 from public TLEs, CelesTrak) and sensor constraints (swath, off-nadir limits, day/night for EO, revisit), offers options with timing (collect -> downlink -> product latency), the human picks; it flows through the Phase C intent pipeline (new intent kinds e.g. collect, cover). Satellite SATCOM passes also drive the link emulator's satcom class and GNSS availability. UI: theater map shows footprints/swaths during passes and link lines; a linked globe view shows orbits; a timeline (access windows per satellite over the area) is the primary space view, because for satellites 'when' matters more than 'where'. Not modeled: satellite bus control, CCSDS, ground-station scheduling internals. Discussed with the user 2026-10-02.

title: Lost-link restore owed by an expended platform stays UNRESTORED forever
description: Seen in the passkeys live run (rules 10 branch, 2026-10-05): an expended switchblade never answered the lost-link restore after its engagement, so replay reports UNRESTORED and the restore stays owed (inbox restore_pending, carried to the next run via .last-run). An expended (consumed) platform can't be restored; decide how the ledger closes it (e.g. an operator writes it off, logged, or the expended state closes the debt automatically with the reason), and make replay agree. Earlier behaviour, not from the passkeys change.

title: Keep-out reach facts fail open for young tracks
description: Focused check of rules 9 (80d8469): a track under about 45 s old has no mean velocity, and one with no manoeuvre seen yet gets no manoeuvre region, so the keep-out falls back to the rules 8 single region (engage.rs track_reach). Stated in doc comments. Consider failing closed: treat a young track as possibly manoeuvring (reach at its domain's plausible top speed) until the facts exist. Needs the next rules version.

title: Fix the scripted-operator set at run start (run.started) so replay checks each session against it
description: Re-check of the auth branch (e5ccf91): whether an operator is scripted is read from the credential file at each login and not recorded in run.started. Turning it off mid-run (murmur-auth scripted <op> off) ends that operator's sessions and the next login logs as 'password', so replay lists them under people; rewriting a session's 'password' as 'scripted' or back passes replay (forgery 14), caught only by anchors. Eval is unaffected (counts only op-study). Fix: log the scripted ids in run.started and have replay check each session's method against them (next rules version). Cosmetic, same review: when the per-session step-up limit trips, the 429 says 'too many failed attempts for this operator' though the limit is per session.

title: After a crash, lost-link values carried from the earlier run's log hold no queued mission
description: Rules 7 (murmur-85l) holds a mission for a platform still owed its own lost-link values by an engagement of this run. Values carried from an earlier run's log (by empty, replay.rs ~269) hold nothing, because the log alone can't tell which vehicle they were preloaded on. So in exactly the crash case, a queued mission carried into the next run can fly over the preloaded fallback. The bridge already checks identity for carried restores; a bridge-fed hold for matching identities (with replay able to recompute it from logged facts) looks possible. Needs a rules version.

title: E2E harnesses predate the rules 5 queue: approve queued orders, expect a submerged AUV patrol to go out
description: Found fixing murmur-0u7: sim/tests/standins_e2e.py approved an order the rules 5 queue was holding (202 queued; approving it is a 409). Its task() was fixed on the murmur-0u7 branch to approve only pending_approval and wait for a queued intent's tasking, but it still can't pass end to end: its second REMUS patrol, sent while submerged by design, is queued on the acoustic-modem link for up to 900 s (DECISIONS 'Reachable means heard'), so the harness's 10-02 expectation must change (expect queued, then surface, then dispatched, or assert the queue reason). The three SITL harnesses (standins_e2e_air.py, standins_e2e_plane_boat_sub.py, standins_e2e_blimp_ugv_sailboat.py) still approve any order without a tasking id and need the same task() fix; run them with SITL to confirm.
notes: From the re-check of 4c42d89: if approving a pending_approval intent puts it in the queue, the approve reply's tasking is null (api.rs ~319-324); standins_e2e.py and standins_tracker_e2e.py then fail on t['id'] instead of waiting. Fall through to the wait when tasking is null.

title: Bridge: name the .last-run log and its head in run.started so dropped carried restores are detectable
description: Review of the replay strictness branch (3ed31ba): replay can't detect a successor log with every carried platform.restore removed (forgery C3: exit 0, nothing said), because nothing in the log says a carry was due. Have the bridge record in run.started which .last-run log it read and that log's head (and whether it owed anything), so replay can require the carried restores. Changes what is logged: needs a rules version. Also from the same review: .last-run is rewritten even when the carry failed (crates/murmur-bridge/src/decision/engage.rs ~756), so an earlier log's debt drops out of the chain with only an inbox alert; keep pointing at the log still owed until its debt is carried or explicitly written off by an operator. And a bridge crash mid carry_from loop (engage.rs ~765-790) leaves a partial carried set, which replay's 'every owed platform carried' would reject: make the carry atomic or log it as one event.
notes: Also from the re-check of f070f5f: the bridge's restore carry (engage.rs carry_restores) trusts the .last-run log without replaying it or checking its anchors, unlike carry_over; murmur-replay can't check the carried values' log against its own anchors in the same run (a <stem>.anchors lookup or --prev-anchors would close forgery N1: predecessor rewritten and re-chained to owe the forged values, caught only by its anchors).

title: A queued newer order abandons an engagement's intercept as a system stop and flies the fallback
description: Final review of rules 6 (present on master 5444976, not from the merge). A newer order queued for an engagement's platform makes supersede_queued abandon the engagement's unstarted intercept (crates/murmur-bridge/src/decision/queue.rs around 239); the engagement loop reads that as an intercept failure (engage.rs around 970), stops with cause 'system: the platform's intercept failed: abandoned ... (the newest order stands)' and commands its fallback. The same order dispatched instead stops it as 'superseded' with no fallback. Probe: a hold queued on a cut link aborted the engagement as system and its fallback RTL flew when the link returned while the operator's hold was still queued (log replays). The stop cause is mislabeled for evaluation (Phase G counts causes) and the operator's order is contradicted until it leaves the queue. Fix: treat a queued newer order like a dispatched one (superseded, no fallback), or decide explicitly and record it in DECISIONS.md.
close_reason: Merged as decision rules 7 (QUEUE_FOLLOWUPS_SINCE) after review, re-check and a third check: starts logged ahead; missions held (or refused for never-queued kinds) while a platform is owed its own lost-link values; an order queued, dispatched or refused for an engaging platform supersedes it without fallback; engine refuses requeue after a start; airship refusal text corrected.

title: Replay --prev doesn't check carried platform.restore values against what the predecessor owed
description: Final review of rules 6: --prev verifies intent.resumed only; carried platform.restore values (crates/murmur-decide/src/replay.rs around 390) are not compared with what the predecessor still owed. The two pointers can name different logs (.resume-<port>.json is deleted on a clean stop and has a 900 s window; .last-run-<port> is rewritten at every start, including MURMUR_RESUME=<log> or =0). Fix: when --prev is the log a carried restore names, check its values against owed_restores(prev).
close_reason: Merged (f070f5f) after review and re-check: replay rejects an op requeued after its start went out (per delivery; adopted vehicles after a resume too) and checks carried platform.restore values against the log they name, which must itself replay; absent or unnamed predecessors fail closed unless --trust-resumed.

title: Refusal reason should name an older queued order that still stands on the same vehicles
description: Third check of rules 7 (486fc49): a mission refused because its platform is still owed its own lost-link values supersedes engagements but leaves older queued orders in place (safer when the older order is a hold or rtl). Under dispatch semantics the newer order would have voided it; here the refusal text doesn't tell the operator the older order still stands. Add a clause naming it.
